title: OpenAI's Atlas Browser Stops Working August 9. The Agent Moves Into ChatGPT and Codex.
desc: OpenAI is deprecating Atlas on August 9, 2026 and moving browser agents into ChatGPT and Codex. Bookmarks, tabs and history do not transfer automatically.
keywords: openai atlas shutdown, chatgpt atlas deprecated, atlas browser august 9 2026, ai browser agent, browser automation ai, openai codex browser, agent vendor risk
cta: Want browser workflows built somewhere they will not be retired?
body:
August 3, 2026. OpenAI's Atlas browser stops working on August 9. The company refreshed its deprecation notice over the weekend, and the short version for anyone who built work around it is that the agent survives, the browser does not, and none of your data moves by itself.

What OpenAI said

  1. Atlas is deprecated and the capability moves. OpenAI's help centre notice, updated August 2, says browser based agentic capabilities are moving into ChatGPT and Codex.
  2. The hard date is August 9, 2026. After that, OpenAI says Atlas may no longer open, browse, or support browser based agentic workflows.
  3. The wind down is about 30 days. OpenAI's own FAQ states the planned announcement date was July 9 and describes an approximately 30 day wind down period.
  4. Nothing migrates automatically. Bookmarks, open tabs and browsing history do not transfer. Cookies have export options where available, and OpenAI warns that cookie and session files should be treated as sensitive data.
  5. The replacement is the desktop app and the Chrome extension. OpenAI points users to the new ChatGPT desktop app for multiple tabs, downloads, improved navigation and account login support, and to the ChatGPT Chrome extension or sidebar for help inside an existing browser.

A product retired inside its first year

Atlas launched in October 2025 according to contemporaneous reporting. It is switched off in August 2026. Whatever the strategic reasoning, the number an operator should take away is the one in OpenAI's own FAQ: roughly 30 days of notice for a product people were using to do real work.

That is not a criticism unique to OpenAI, and the direction of travel is easy to read. Agent capability is consolidating out of standalone applications and into two places that are much harder to retire, the assistant itself and the browser extension layer. A separate AI browser was always the part most likely to get absorbed.

The mistake was never trying Atlas. The mistake is building a business process on any single vendor's standalone agent app without first asking what happens when it gets folded into something else.

What it means for operators

  1. Export before Friday if anyone on your team used it. Bookmarks export as an HTML file and import into Chrome. Open tabs and history have to be saved by hand. OpenAI is explicit that none of it moves on its own.
  2. Do not keep using it after the ninth. OpenAI's stated reason for a hard date is that a discontinued browser stops receiving security maintenance. A browser is not something to run unpatched to save a migration.
  3. Ask every agent vendor what notice period they give. Thirty days is now a real answer in this market. That question belongs alongside pricing and uptime, and it is entirely fair to ask for it in writing before you commit a workflow.
  4. Prefer the layer that has a migration path. Work built on an API, a protocol or an extension survives a product being renamed or absorbed. Work built inside one vendor's application does not.

If a browser task is load bearing in your business, it should live somewhere you control the migration path. That is the practical argument for building it as AI automation you own rather than as a habit inside somebody else's app, and it is the first question we ask when we put an AI engineer on a client workflow.
faqs: When exactly does OpenAI Atlas stop working?

Atlas is scheduled to stop working on August 9, 2026. OpenAI states that after that date Atlas may no longer open, browse, or support browser based agentic workflows, and that users should move to a supported browser experience before then.
Will my Atlas bookmarks, tabs and history transfer to ChatGPT?

No. OpenAI states that bookmarks will not transfer automatically and that open tabs and browsing history may not transfer either. Export bookmarks to an HTML file and import them into another browser such as Chrome, and save any pages you need before August 9, 2026. ChatGPT conversation history is separate from Atlas browser data and is unaffected.
What replaces Atlas for browser based AI work?

OpenAI directs users to the ChatGPT desktop app, which it says supports multiple tabs, downloads, improved navigation and account login support, and to the ChatGPT Chrome extension or sidebar where available. Availability can depend on your plan, region, device, browser and workspace settings.
What should a business learn from an AI product being retired inside a year?

Ask any agent vendor what notice period they give before retiring a product, and prefer to build workflows on an API, protocol or extension rather than inside a single vendor's standalone application. OpenAI's own FAQ describes an approximately 30 day wind down for Atlas, which is a useful benchmark for how fast this category moves.
